taskpack.goal: Implement durable, replay-stable usage attribution for every supported Codex-backed model invocation, including start-before-launch lifecycle authority, provider-session lineage, projection, reporting, and deterministic acceptance.
taskpack.integration_policy: verified integration baseline followed by operator review

tasks.objective: Define machine-valid invocation start, terminal usage, and live-smoke schemas; implement strict provider JSONL parsing without cumulative double counting or guessed session deltas.
tasks.goal_alignment: Freezes the accounting contract used by every later capture, projection, and acceptance task.
acceptance_criteria: Start and terminal schemas validate stable IDs, immutable prelaunch coverage class, dual session identities, optional implementation-run and gate-epoch correlation, UTC timestamps, token constraints, and unavailable reasons.

A supported live start requires Linger=yes, the enclosing system-level user service InvocationID, ControlGroup, and cleanup-capable KillMode, plus the exact transient-service unit, InvocationID, user-manager identity, and ControlGroup; not-applicable adapters do not invent them.
Live-smoke commit fields validate as Git OIDs for the declared repository object format rather than fixed-length file SHA-256 digests.
The live-smoke schema binds its attempt-scoped evidence run to run_kind acceptance_evidence, the logical implementation run, and one gate epoch.
Repeated cumulative provider snapshots produce one final usage total.

Ambiguous, resume_last cumulative, missing-predecessor, missing provider-turn continuity, concurrent, forked, or non-monotonic session usage is partial or unavailable rather than guessed; its per-invocation token fields are null and it cannot contribute a lower bound.
The canonical event enum declares invocation start, writer revocation, and terminal usage events before scheduler tasks emit them.
Revocation records bind one invocation and exact owner token and cannot be rewritten for a different owner.
Cached and reasoning fields do not inflate provider total tokens.
Legacy parser and aggregation tests remain compatible.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop before adapter changes if the installed provider fixture cannot identify a terminal usage payload without guessing.

tasks.objective: Persist a durable invocation start before every Codex worker launch attempt and finalize exactly one terminal usage record for every controlled outcome.
tasks.goal_alignment: Prevents provider calls from disappearing after crashes and captures real cost on failure and timeout paths.
acceptance_criteria: A gated supervisor cannot launch the provider until its PID, PGID, boot ID, process start ticks, owner token, launch nonce digest, and exact transient-service identity are durable in the start record.
The supervisor remains the process-group leader through provider terminalization, installs the supported Linux parent-death safeguard, and kills/reaps the group on abnormal exit.

The supervisor launches only inside a uniquely identified systemd user transient service with RemainAfterExit and control-group kill semantics under a lingering, identity-bound user service; PGID-only fallback is forbidden.

Parent death before durable start closes the permit channel without a provider call; death after durable start but before permit becomes one recoverable launch_failed; death after permit leaves a PID-reuse-safe fenceable identity.

Recovery distinguishes changed host boot, live pinned pidfd, and same-boot reaped supervisor: ESRCH alone never proves death, and the exact transient-service ControlGroup must report cgroup.events populated 0 or be stopped and observed at populated 0.

A completed enclosing user-service restart with a changed InvocationID and cleanup-capable persisted KillMode proves the old manager lifetime dead without signaling; an unexplained inner-manager identity change remains open.
Every controlled terminal outcome has one idempotent terminal usage record.
Provider process ownership and terminal writer tokens are bounded and terminal creation is exclusive.
Normal and recovery finalizers share one invocation lock; revocation is durable under that lock and a revoked old writer cannot publish a competing terminal.
A post-start crash leaves a discoverable open invocation for recovery.
Missing, recycled, or ambiguous systemd unit, manager, or control-group identity remains open rather than signaling or terminalizing an unrelated process.
Timeout after usage preserves provider totals; timeout before usage is unavailable with a bounded reason.
Retries have distinct invocation IDs and untrusted session snapshots never overcount.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if durable process and execution-group identity cannot precede launch, the required Linux pidfd/systemd authority is unavailable, or terminal capture would require unbounded subprocess logs.

tasks.objective: Propagate lifecycle and session context through mailbox and scheduler paths, serialize cumulative provider-session writers, and reconcile dead orphaned invocations.
tasks.goal_alignment: Makes durable worker capture survive process boundaries, retries, replay, and scheduler recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Every supported worker route supplies explicit stage and lifecycle context.
Snapshot and predecessor identity cross mailbox boundaries byte-equivalently.
A dead fenced orphan becomes one recovery terminal invocation while lease expiry with a live process remains open.

Recovery emits the predeclared writer-revocation event and follows the changed-boot, live-pidfd, or same-boot reaped-supervisor decision tree; it acts only on a pinned pidfd or the exact verified transient service before rereading terminal and bounded-spool evidence.
A supervisor exit and numeric PID reuse between identity comparison and signaling cannot target the replacement process.

ESRCH alone never proves death: the same-boot exact transient-service ControlGroup must report cgroup.events populated 0, while changed-boot or a proved enclosing user-service restart sends no signal and ambiguous identity remains open.

Explicit cumulative provider sessions use a user-level shared lock namespace, immutable first-project binding, bound-project file authority, and provider-turn continuity; cross-project resume is rejected, and unresolved resume_last calls in one provider resume domain are single-flight but never gain authoritative delta lineage from local order.
Replay preserves invocation and usage event IDs and existing recovery tests pass.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if session lineage cannot be propagated and serialized, process death cannot be proven through changed-boot, pinned-pidfd, or exact transient-service authority, or mailbox replay would need a new invocation identity.

tasks.objective: Capture durable start and terminal provider usage for taskpack authors, runtime diagnostic chat, and tracked standalone development-smoke entry points, including failure, timeout, salvage, and recovery paths.
tasks.goal_alignment: Includes every supported non-worker pre-controller provider call in the same invocation-level accounting contract as worker execution.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary and pursue-round-1 author calls use taskpack_author; pursue round 2 and later plus next use follow_up_author; all use the gated-supervisor and transient-service handshake with explicit round attribution.
Runtime diagnostic chat and every tracked standalone development-smoke provider entry point cross the shared lifecycle primitive with explicit stage and a controller-owned runtime execution session.
A source scan and deterministic fixture agree on the closed supported invocation inventory.
Success, failure, timeout, salvage, and changed-boot, live-pidfd, or exact transient-service crash recovery preserve one terminal or open lifecycle as appropriate.
Provider usage is never replaced by prompt_estimated_tokens.
Failed author calls remain discoverable even without a frozen taskpack or run directory.
A successful submit writes one bounded author lifecycle bootstrap below the run before scheduler launch, with work-root-relative contained paths and fixed record digests.
Ordinary draft and taskpack cleanup preserves non-rebuildable author lifecycle authority; destructive removal is explicit and reports canonical-import status and accounting loss.
Existing custom-command and legacy author contexts remain compatible.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if a supported non-worker provider entry point cannot cross the shared lifecycle boundary without breaking its interactive, custom-command, or timeout-salvage contract.

tasks.objective: Import invocation starts and terminal usage into canonical events with idempotent replay, conflict detection, provider predecessor reconstruction, and open-lifecycle preservation.
tasks.goal_alignment: Creates replayable file authority without counting artifact replay as additional model cost.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical start and terminal event imports are idempotent and preserve source IDs.
The scheduler validates the author bootstrap path containment and record digests before worker dispatch; bootstrap replay does not duplicate cost.
Duplicate byte-equivalent records count once and conflicting records fail integrity checks.
An open start remains visible through replay.
Provider predecessor and snapshot reconstruction uses provider_session_id, never runtime execution order.
Historical event logs are not rewritten.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if replayability requires destructive event migration or replacing file authority with mutable database state.

tasks.objective: Aggregate canonical invocation lifecycles into compact terminal and Feishu reports while preserving reported, partial, unavailable, not-applicable, and open states.
tasks.goal_alignment: Makes full-run usage understandable without raw logs or task-level undercounting.
acceptance_criteria: Reports include author and worker invocations and distinguish invocation count from completed task count.
Reported, partial, unavailable, not-applicable, and open states remain distinct.
Exact reported totals are labeled as subset totals when token coverage is below 100 percent, with only invocation-scoped partial fields shown as lower bounds and ambiguous session snapshots excluded.
Open invocations block completion and 100 percent coverage.
Terminal and Feishu summaries render the same compact aggregate values.
Legacy summaries are labeled and never mixed into benchmark totals.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if reporting requires mutating canonical events or treating missing historical usage as zero.

tasks.objective: Project authoritative starts and terminals into rebuildable SQLite rows and expose invocation-level coverage and attribution through agentteam stats.
tasks.goal_alignment: Enables exact cost and coverage queries while retaining files as authority.
acceptance_criteria: Projection left-joins terminals onto unique starts and uses starts as the coverage denominator.
Fresh DB and authoritative file scan have identical counts, digests, coverage, and token totals.
Deleting and rebuilding the DB is stable and corrupt or stale DB falls back to files with a warning.
Controller acceptance artifacts are discovered only under the configured project work_root/runs tree.
Acceptance evidence runs remain explicitly queryable and included in milestone aggregation but cannot replace the default latest implementation run.
Open recovery changes lifecycle status without changing invocation count, and session-cumulative ambiguous snapshots never enter projected lower bounds.
Stats filters preserve authority and legacy runs cannot silently pass benchmark coverage.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if SQL would need to repair missing capture records or fresh-DB and file-fallback semantics cannot be identical.

tasks.objective: Build a positive deterministic end-to-end fixture for complete usage coverage and a separate negative fixture for safely fenced crash recovery, projection rebuild, filters, and replay.
tasks.goal_alignment: Proves complete positive accounting without hiding the intentionally unavailable token usage in the recovery fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture covers every supported pre-controller author, planner, repo-map, implementation, review, semantic, follow-up, runtime-diagnostic, and tracked development-smoke path.
The positive fixture has exact predeclared counts and totals, 100 percent lifecycle and token coverage, and zero open invocations.
The separate recovery fixture transitions from lifecycle/token 0/1 with one open invocation to lifecycle 1/1, token 0/1, and zero open without changing the denominator.
Lease expiry while the process is live does not terminalize the recovery fixture.

The reaped-supervisor recovery path terminalizes only after exact transient-service control-group empty proof; changed-boot, proved enclosing user-service restart, and ambiguous same-boot cases are covered separately.
Two replay and projection rebuild passes are identical and the full discovery suite passes.
tasks.stop_condition: Do not pass with incomplete positive coverage, unexpected negative-fixture metrics, projection drift, or recovery that erases or prematurely closes a start.

tasks.objective: Implement a bounded live-smoke helper and independent deterministic controller that alone can atomically publish the fixed acceptance artifact.
tasks.goal_alignment: Makes the real provider compatibility gate executable and prevents worker prose or the production parser from self-validating success.
acceptance_criteria: Only the deterministic controller can atomically publish the fixed success artifact.
Controller and imported Phase 1 modules resolve from the candidate integration worktree rather than the old active release.
Controller validation independently decodes the bounded provider spool rather than reusing token_usage.py.
Start and terminal records share one invocation ID and provider hash and totals reconcile exactly.
An isolated projection of the staged candidate passes before the fixed authoritative artifact is published.
The controller derives its run directory below the configured project work_root so projection can discover the final artifact.
The controller loads the profile from an explicit source checkout, validates a separate candidate worktree in the same Git common directory, and does not require .agentteam inside that candidate.

Before gate registration or provider launch, the controller durably stages run identity plus immutable owner/commit/series/attempt claim and publishes the complete attempt run with one Linux no-replace directory rename; check-then-create is forbidden.
The controller durably writes run_identity.v1.json with run_kind acceptance_evidence and the logical taskpack and implementation run IDs before registration or launch.
Every real retry uses a fresh immutable acceptance run ID; incomplete-run reopening is recovery-only, passed-run lookup is idempotent, and failed attempts remain attributed.
The helper, lifecycle records, projection row, and final artifact all use the same attempt-scoped run ID derived from acceptance series and attempt IDs.
Claim, run identity, lifecycle records, projection row, fixed artifact, and receipt agree on the logical implementation run and current gate epoch; a stale epoch fails before provider launch.
The implementation-run gate receipt is pending before publication and resolves only from the validated fixed artifact.

Fake-command tests cover authorization, malformed data, mismatches, oversized output, dirty or changed source, projection rejection, interrupted publish, retry IDs, idempotent passed lookup, and concurrent same-ID claims with exactly one provider launch.
One epoch/gate execution lock prevents concurrent different-attempt live calls, and an open invocation from a crashed attempt blocks replacement until safe recovery.
The live controller retains both run-level and epoch/gate locks, then rereads epoch, claims, open invocations, Git refs, and worktree state under lock before provider launch.
Normal unit tests never make a live provider call or write into the candidate worktree.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if helper or worker claims can publish success, independent validation is not independent, or the live call can mutate candidate source.

tasks.objective: Implement deterministic milestone report rendering and external finalization that verifies the report-only commit lineage without a self-referential source commit SHA.
tasks.goal_alignment: Makes the post-live merge recommendation reproducible and binds validated code to a narrowly scoped report-only integration commit.
acceptance_criteria: Report rendering is byte-stable and accepts only canonical deterministic and P1-LIVE evidence.
Renderer and finalizer functions resolve from the Phase 1 integration worktree rather than the old active release.
The report uses explicit acceptance-series metadata and includes usage from every failed, incomplete, retried, and selected live attempt.
The source report records validated_code_sha and evidence digests but never attempts to contain its own commit SHA.
The source report and roadmap remain finalization_pending and make only a conditional merge recommendation.
Renderer requires a clean validated_code_sha head, writes and commits only the fixed report and roadmap paths, and returns the single-parent final_report_sha without source-merge authority.

One complete controller holds both run-level and P1-06E epoch/gate execution locks across pending registration, report commit, validation, and final artifact publication, rereads all preconditions under lock, and rejects a stale epoch before source mutation.
Finalization requires a clean single-parent head whose parent is validated_code_sha and whose diff contains only the fixed report and roadmap paths.
Wrong parent, extra path, evidence mismatch, dirty status, and report tampering all fail closed.

Renderer and finalizer load the profile from the explicit source checkout, validate the separate candidate worktree in the same Git common directory, and use the same configured project work_root and registered acceptance run as P1-LIVE.
Only a passed internal finalizer atomically publishes the external schema-valid finalization artifact.
A crash after the report-only commit is resumable only when that exact clean child and pending receipt match byte-stable output for the same evidence; retry never creates a second report commit.
A byte-equivalent retry after passed finalization returns idempotently without a second report commit or completion notification.
Finalization commit fields validate as Git OIDs for the declared repository object format.

The implementation-run P1-06E gate remains pending before publication, becomes awaiting_operator_review when final_report_sha equals the integration head, and passes only after matching immutable operator approval.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if canonical evidence cannot drive the report, finalization becomes self-referential, or the controller would need source-branch merge authority.

tasks.objective: Document the implemented invocation accounting, stats filters, lifecycle states, database authority boundary, live gate, report renderer, and finalizer commands.
tasks.goal_alignment: Provides an operator surface that matches verified behavior without claiming the live or finalization gates have already passed.
acceptance_criteria: Commands and fields match the implemented CLI and schemas.
Documentation explains provider-token units, cached and reasoning fields, coverage, open and legacy states, and DB projection authority.
The exact live controller, report completion, and digest-bound interactive operator approval commands are documented.
No document claims Phase 1 complete before P1-LIVE, finalization evidence, and operator approval pass.
All referenced links and paths resolve.
tasks.stop_condition: Stop if implementation evidence and requested documentation disagree; do not weaken the contract to hide the mismatch.
